newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish state auditors say NFIs managers overpaid.
newsitem.headline: Polish state auditors say NFIs managers overpaid.

text.p: Poland's Supreme Auditing Chamber (NIK) said on Wednesday it would probe all National Investment Funds (NFIs) after it found management wages to be too high in five of the country's 15 mass privatisation funds.
NIK president Janusz Wojciechowski told a news conference that salaries in NFI funds Nos. 1, 3, 4, 9 and 13 were excessive.
Wojciechowski said that during the first and second quarter of 1995 wages for management firms for NFIs No. 3, 9 and 12 were excessive by a total of about 2.8 million zlotys.
The NIK report said the firms managing these funds ought to have been paid less because they were put in charge of smaller number of companies than originally assumed.

Under Poland's mass privatisation programme, consortia of international and domestic banks and consulting firms are running most the scheme's 15 funds, which were given strategic stakes in 512 medium-size companies.
Wojciechowski said that NIK did not find problems in the distribution mass privatisation certificates, during which some 95 percent of the 28 million eligible Poles bought such unit.
Each NFI unit will be exchanged this year into 15 shares, one in each of the 15 NFI funds embracing about 500 small and medium-sized companies, which will then enter the Warsaw bourse.
